body.p: REMARKS
This communication is responsive to the Final Office Action dated April 29, 2024.
Applicant has amended claims 1, 18, 27, and 29. Claims 1, 3-5, 7, 8, 10, 11, 13-18, 20, 21, 23, 24, and 26-32 remain pending.
Applicant respectfully requests entry of the claim amendments after issuance of the Final Office Action. The claim amendments are clerical, and require no further search or consideration.
The Office Action rejected claims 1, 3-5, 7, 8, 10, 11, 13-18, 20, 21, 23, 24, and 26-32 under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as follows:

Applicant respectfully traverses the rejections. The applied references, alone or in any combination, fail to disclose or suggest the features defined by Applicant's claims, and there would have been no apparent reason that would have caused one of ordinary skill in the art to modify the applied references to arrive at the claimed features.
For example, the applied references fail to disclose or suggest a system comprising
"processing circuitry of at least one of [an] insertable cardiac monitor or [a] remote computing device, the processing circuitry configured to: periodically determine a respective value for each

of a plurality of physiological parameters based on one or more of [] heart sounds or [an] ECG, wherein at least a first physiological parameter of the plurality of physiological parameters is determined based on the heart sounds and at least a second physiological parameter of the plurality of physiological parameters is determined based on the ECG, wherein the first physiological parameter comprises a frequency of occurrence of an S3 heart sound; ... and determine whether to present an indication of a heart failure event based on an analysis of the trends of the periodically determined values of the physiological parameters, wherein to perform the analysis of the trends the processing circuitry is configured to: determine a first variation value of at least one physiological parameter of the plurality of physiological parameters for a first period and a second variation value of the at least one physiological parameter for a second period preceding the first period; and determine whether a comparison of the first variation value and the second variation value satisfies a criterion,"1 as recited by amended independent claim 1, or the similar recitations of amended independent claims 18, 27, and 29.
The Office Action acknowledged that "Stahmann modified by McCabe, Zhang, and

Siejko ... does not disclose .. processing circuitry is configured to: determine a first variation value of at least one physiological parameter of the plurality of physiological parameters for a first period and a second variation value of the at least one of the physiological parameter for a second period preceding the first period; and determine whether a comparison of the first variation value and the second variation value satisfies a criterion."2 The Office Action asserted "Gheeraert teaches an ECG analysis system that takes ECG data and compares it to a previous sequence of consecutive data for a patient based on different conditions in the form of difference vectors and provides a signal representative of a risk of myocardial infarction (eg. Abstract, Para. 31-32, 86, 172-176)."3 The Office Action argued "[i]t would have been obvious ... to have combined the invention of Stahmann, McCabe, Zhang, and Siejko with the difference vector analysis as taught by Gheeraert to improve assessment with low sensitivity to false positives (eg. Gheeraert, Para. 18-30)."4
Applicant respectfully disagrees. Gheeraert describes "calculating a difference vector of the three ST levels with respect to a reference vector . .. obtained by calculating an average of a
1 Emphasis added.
2 Final Office Action dated April 29, 2024, pg. 5.
3 Final Office Action dated April 29, 2024, pp. 5-6.
4 Final Office Action dated April 29, 2024, pg. 6.

plurality of dipole measurements ... [and] generating a signal taking into account this comparison, for example a signal representative of a risk of myocardial infarction occurring in the body of the user."5 However, neither the difference vector, nor the reference vector, is a variation value for a period. Instead, per Gheeraert, the vectors are three-dimensional coordinate representations of three ST levels from three dipoles.6 Consequentially, any comparison of these vectors, e.g., a vector difference, is not comparison of a first variation value and a second variation value, per Applicant's claims.

Furthermore, as acknowledged in the Office Action,7 Gheeraert describes techniques for determining a risk of myocardial infarction,8 and does not appear to suggest that its techniques would be useful for determining whether to present an indication of a heart failure event. As such, even if a person of ordinary skill in the art considered the techniques described by Gheeraert to provide low sensitivity to false positives as suggested in the Office Action, the Office Action does not establish that such a person would have considered it obvious to utilize these techniques to whether to determine whether to "present an indication of a heart failure event," as recited in Applicant's claims.

For at least these reasons, the Office has failed to establish aprimafacie case for non- patentability of Applicant's claims under 35 U.S.C. § 103. Applicant therefore respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of this rejection.

CONCLUSION
All claims in this application are in condition for allowance. Applicant does not

acquiesce as to any assertion in the Office Action with respect to the cited art or to Applicant's claims. Applicant's silence with respect to any assertion in the Office Action should not be interpreted as Applicant's acquiescence thereto. Applicant reserves the right to comment further with respect to the applied references and any pending claim in a future Amendment, Response, or on appeal. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and prompt allowance of all pending claims.

Applicant does not concede that the subject matter encompassed by the claims prior to this Response is unpatentable over the art cited by the Office Action. While several distinctions have been noted over the art of record, Applicant notes that there may be several other limitations that are neither taught nor suggested by the art of record. Applicant expressly reserves all rights and arguments with respect to distinctions not explicitly noted herein. In addition, to the extent that amendments included herein constitute a narrowing of the claims, such narrowing of the claims should not be construed as an admission as to the merits of the prior rejections. Indeed, Applicant traverses the rejections and preserves all rights and arguments. To the extent that any particular statement or argument by the Office in the pending Office Action has not been explicitly addressed herein, the same should not be construed as an acquiescence or admission by the Applicant that such statements or arguments by the Office are accurate and proper. Further, Applicant does not concede that the art of record is relevant to the subject matter of the claims or analogous art.
